newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia govt accused over opposition municipalities.
newsitem.headline: Serbia govt accused over opposition municipalities.

text.p: Serbia's opposition on Sunday accused the central government of cutting budget funding to cities and town where opposition forces won recent local elections.

"We received the 1997 municipal draft budget, which shows that the funds for all municipalities in which we have won have been cut down, This is simply illegal," opposition leader Zoran Djindjic told a Belgrade gathering of recently elected opposition officials.

"This is a crime to punish the citizens who voted for the opposition. It's an assault on the elementary civic right -- freedom of choice...this regime has lost its head, its compass, and is behaving like an elephant in a glass shop."

Djindjic would be Mayor of Belgrade today if his victory in November's local balloting had not been overturned by an election council controlled by Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and his ruling SPS party.

The opposition leader appeared at a Sunday meeting of the Association of Free Cities and Municipalities, a collection of other opposition figures who, like himself, won local elections but have been barred from taking power.

An opposition coalition known as Zajedno (Together) has been coordinating street protests in Belgrade and other cities and towns across Serbia for the past 35 days in a bid to force Milosevic to honour election results.
Djindjic insisted formation of the Association of Free Cities and Municipalities did not represent an attempt to establish a parallel set of authorities in disputed localities.
"We want regular power in Serbia, not parallel authorities," he said.
